reads_as_reason: Smooth, well-faired blanks, but a slab-like constant-width thigh with soap-bar end radii and a bare cut knee make it a clean prototype rather than a shaped product.

G1.evidence: Thigh reads as a tombstone/bar-of-soap slab; sides near-parallel, same large radius at both ends. Agrees with failed P8a 0.708 and S4a 0.4341. The shank's calf bulge and ankle narrowing are closer to adult proportions.

G2.evidence: Flow inside each segment is good (long continuous zebra bands). The knee is an abrupt horizontal gap with an angled cut (flat elliptical disc in the back view, knife-point at the rear in the side view); recess colour not rendered.

G3.evidence: Single-tone clay; the knee gap is the only place a dark recess could go and it is a plain flat gap with no pocket geometry.

G4.evidence: Similar rounded-rectangle section and edge radii on both segments, seam lines on the same plane, silhouette follows the target.

G6.evidence: No references. Calf swell and rear-biased shank match that family; slab thigh with no distal narrowing or knee-cap form does not. Leaning no-match.

pairwise.evidence: Candidate has fair, continuous zebra bands and a silhouette on the target outline. Baseline has blotchy zebra, dents and a wobbly waisted shank, and bulges outside the red target at knee and calf. Both share the same cut knee interface.

top_changes.change: Taper the thigh visibly from hip to knee; narrow the distal end so it stops reading as a parallel-sided bar.
Break up the broad flat faces by lowering section squareness mid-segment (S4a).
Stronger calf-to-ankle taper; soften the knife-edge rear tip of the shank top and shape the knee as a deliberate recess or cap.

notes: Station names are the critic's guesses. 65 and 130 degree views show no visible collision.
